questions.context:
When Marta was twelve, her family moved from the city to a small farm in the mountains. At first she hated it. There were no cinemas, no shopping centres, and her new school was twenty minutes away by bus. She missed her old friends terribly.

Everything changed the summer she met Tomas, a boy from the next farm who kept bees with his grandfather. He showed her how the bees lived and worked, and Marta was fascinated. By the end of the summer, she knew more about bees than most adults. Her grandfather gave her an old notebook, and she began writing down everything she saw in the fields.

Years later, Marta is a scientist who studies how climate change affects insects. She travels around the world giving talks, but she still lives near her childhood farm. 'The bees taught me to be patient and to watch carefully,' she says. 'And the mountains taught me that quiet places can be the most interesting ones.' She still keeps the old notebook — now almost full — on her desk.
questions.stem: How did Marta feel when she first moved to the farm?
options: Unhappy, because she missed her old life.
Excited about living in the mountains.
Bored because there was nothing to do.
questions.explanation: The text says she hated it at first and missed her old friends.

tasks.title: Mock 1 · Part 1: Reply to Kate's email
tasks.rubric: Read the email from your English friend Kate. Write a reply answering all four points (about 100 words).
tasks.inputText:
Hi!
Guess what — my family is coming to visit your town next weekend!
We'll arrive by train around noon on Saturday. Can you meet us at the station? Where should we go first in the afternoon — somewhere outdoors, maybe? And we'd love to try local food — do you know a good restaurant?
Also, what time do people usually have dinner in your town?
See you soon!
Kate
points: Say if you can meet them at the station
Suggest an outdoor place for the afternoon
Recommend a restaurant for local food
Say what time people usually have dinner
tasks.model:
Hi Kate,

What great news! I'd love to meet you at the station on Saturday — I'll be there at noon, don't worry.

In the afternoon, why don't we walk around the old town and climb the hill to the castle? The view is amazing, and it's free.

For dinner, I recommend The Garden — it serves traditional dishes from our region, and the prices are reasonable. You must try the vegetable soup!

People here usually have dinner between seven and eight, so eight o'clock would be perfect.

Looking forward to seeing you!

Ana
tasks.modelNotes: All four points answered in order; 'why don't we' gives a suggestion; 'looking forward to seeing' adds range.
checklist: All four content points are answered

tasks.title: Mock 1 · Part 2: The door was open
tasks.rubric: Your teacher has asked you to write a story beginning with the words 'The door was open'. Write your story (about 100 words).
points: End with a feeling or lesson
tasks.model:
The door was open, and that was strange — I always lock it before school. I stood in the hallway, listening. Was someone in the house?

I walked slowly towards the kitchen. Suddenly, I heard a noise behind me. I turned around fast... and saw my little sister, smiling.

'Surprise!' she said. 'I made you a birthday cake!'

On the table there was a chocolate cake with my name on it. It wasn't perfect — one side was burnt — but it was the best present I had ever had.

I hugged her and laughed. I'll never forget that afternoon.
tasks.modelNotes: Opens with the required words, uses past tenses and 'suddenly', resolves clearly, ends with feeling.
checklist: Story begins with the given words
There is a clear problem and resolution

l_m1_p3_main.speaker: M
l_m1_p3_main.text: Hello, and welcome to the Greenfield Adventure Park. I'm Paul, one of the guides, and I'll tell you about what we offer.

l_m1_p3_main.speaker: M
l_m1_p3_main.text: The park opened in 2015, and since then more than fifty thousand visitors have enjoyed our activities. We are open every day from nine in the morning until six in the evening.

l_m1_p3_main.speaker: M
l_m1_p3_main.text: Our most popular activity is the tree-top walk — a path high up in the forest, suitable for everyone over eight years old. For the bravest visitors, we also have a forty-metre zip wire crossing the lake.

l_m1_p3_main.speaker: M
l_m1_p3_main.text: Entry costs twelve pounds for adults and eight pounds for children. Families with two or more children get a twenty percent discount. You can book tickets on our website or by phone on zero-one-six-two-five, seven-seven-four, three-two-one — that's 01625 774321.

l_m1_p3_main.speaker: M
l_m1_p3_main.text: We look forward to seeing you at Greenfield!

l_m1_p4_main.speaker: W
l_m1_p4_main.text: Today I'd like to tell you about an unusual school — the Island School, which is only reachable by boat. About ninety children study there, from six to sixteen years old.

l_m1_p4_main.speaker: W
l_m1_p4_main.text: Every morning, a special school boat collects children from five small villages around the lake. The journey takes between ten and twenty-five minutes, depending on the village. The children love it — many of them say it's the best part of their day.

l_m1_p4_main.speaker: W
l_m1_p4_main.text: The school itself is small but modern. Because classes are small, teachers know every student very well. The students do the same subjects as in other schools, but they also learn something special: sailing. Every child learns to sail a boat before they leave, and the school team has won several regional competitions.

l_m1_p4_main.speaker: W
l_m1_p4_main.text: Winter can be difficult. When the lake freezes, the boat cannot run, so the school closes for a few days and students learn from home. But this happens only three or four times a year.

l_m1_p4_main.speaker: W
l_m1_p4_main.text: The head teacher, Mrs Lund, says the school teaches children independence. 'Our students learn to solve problems by themselves,' she says. 'That's a lesson for life.'
